comment: Physical Memory Protection CSRs. They are M-mode registers (csr[9:8]=3 in every address here), so they live in an M-mode block, and they are a separate table because a profile without a less-privileged mode implements no PMP entries at all and must not be given these numbers.

csrs.name: pmpcfg0
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033. src/machine.tex section 'Physical Memory Protection' L3336 and '2.7.1 Physical Memory Protection CSRs' L3396: 'The PMP configuration registers are densely packed into CSRs... For RV64, eight even-numbered CSRs, pmpcfg0, pmpcfg2, ..., pmpcfg14, hold the configurations for the 64 PMP entries... For RV64, the odd-numbered configuration registers, pmpcfg1, pmpcfg3, ..., pmpcfg15, are illegal.' Address 0x3A0 (pmpcfg0) and 0x3A2 (pmpcfg2) from src/priv-csrs.tex Table 'CSR number assignments' ('0x3A0 & MRW & pmpcfg0', '0x3A2 & MRW & pmpcfg2') with the profile's own entry count of 16 from config/geometry/p1.json. Field layout Figure 'PMP configuration register format': per byte, bit 7 L, bit 6:5 reserved, bit 4:3 A, bit 2 X, bit 1 W, bit 0 R; 'All PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero'. The reserved bits are declared unmodifiable (they read zero) and every other bit is writable subject to the lock rule, which is dynamic and therefore not expressible as a static mask: 'If PMP entry i is locked, writes to pmp_i cfg and pmpaddr_i are ignored', and 'The R, W, and X fields form a collective WARL field for which the combinations with R=0 and W=1 are reserved'. rtl/core/mosaic_pmp.sv is the one place that rule lives. Entries 0-7 live in this register.

csrs.name: pmpaddr0
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033. src/machine.tex '2.7.1 Physical Memory Protection CSRs' L3418: 'The PMP address registers are CSRs named pmpaddr0-pmpaddr63. ... For RV64, each PMP address register encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address ... Not all physical address bits may be implemented, and so the pmpaddr registers are WARL.' Addresses 0x3B0-0x3BF from src/priv-csrs.tex Table 'CSR number assignments'. Bits 53:0 are the 54 encoded address bits and bits 63:54 read zero; the grain is 4 bytes (G=0, config/geometry/p1.json), so no low bit is hardwired and NA4 is selectable ('When G >= 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable').
